title: Session fidelity brakepoints and lightweight tool surface PRD
content:
Context and motivation:
We see recurring integration issues when client apps try to consume long-running streaming outputs while also orchestrating tool calls. Clients either overfetch (wasteful) or stop early (losing actions). SDKs today force a binary choice: stream everything raw, or do synchronous tool call turns. This PRD proposes a lightweight session protocol with explicit fidelity brakepoints and a minimal tool surface on the Hosted API SDKs that lets clients trade latency, bandwidth, and action-decision granularity without requiring heavyweight re-architecting of either side.

High level idea:
- Define 'brakepoints' in the incremental output stream: predictable checkpoints where the model/runtime promises a consistent partial state (tokens + structured annotations + KV snapshot markers). Clients can attach policy decisions to brakepoints (e.g., pause/await-tool, prefetch, or continue).
- Surface a tiny SDK primitive (SessionController) that exposes these brakepoints, policy hooks, and a small tool call API that can be implemented with either the hosted tool router or forwarded to customer tools.
- Make brakepoints cheap (a few bytes of metadata) and stable across retries/rollouts so SDKs can resume or replay without losing action semantics.

Goals:
- Reduce accidental tool duplication and spurious tool calls from clients reacting to partial streams.
- Allow clients to implement bandwidth- or latency-sensitive flows: e.g., mobile clients that only want high-confidence action frames, web apps that speculatively prefetch cached results, server-side orchestrators that prefer deterministic handoff points.
- Keep server-side runtime work minimal: brakepoints are markers and don't cause expensive global syncs.
- Backwards-compatible: existing streaming endpoints keep their semantics; new contract is opt-in per-call.

Non-goals:
- Not attempting to solve full distributed orchestration across many agents; this is for single session client-server ergonomics.
- Not a replacement for full transactionality or guaranteed once semantics.

User stories:
- Mobile product: "During a composition flow on flaky networks, show partial summary frames only at brakepoints so UI can snapshot the message without streaming artifacts or mid-word truncation."
- Agent orchestration: "An orchestration service wants deterministic points to decide whether to call an external knowledge tool or wait for more tokens; brakepoints signal safe decision boundaries."
- Low-bandwidth mode: "Client asks for only structural deltas and tool-action candidates at brakepoints; avoid continuous full-text streaming."

API surface sketch (hosted-api):
- request param: session_protocol: {"fidelity": "balanced|low|high", "brakepoint_interval": "auto|n_tokens|time_ms"}  (encoded as standard request JSON/headers)
- response stream includes regular chunks plus special frame types: {"type":"brakepoint","id":"bp-<uuid>","seq":123,"annotations":[...],"kv_snapshot_token":"s-2412"}  
- tool call handshake: {"type":"tool-call-request","bp_id":"bp-<uuid>","tool_suggestions":[{"tool":"search","confidence":0.8, ...}],"caller_metadata":{...}}
- resume token: included in brakepoint frames; allows client to request resume/replay from that exact point on reconnect.

SDK primitives (sketch):
- SessionController.open(opts) -> session
- session.on('brakepoint', (bp) => { // bp.id, textCursor, annotations, resumeToken })
- session.policy = {onBrakepoint(bp, ctx) => CONTINUE | PAUSE | CALL_TOOL}
- session.callTool(toolName, payload, opts) -> Promise(actionResult)  // lightweight client wrapper that calls hosted routing or emits an event for host app forwarding
- session.resume(resumeToken)

SDK ergonomics notes:
- Keep the high-level API minimal: many teams misuse heavy event systems; prefer a callback + policy return enum.
- Provide platform-specific helpers: mobile SDKs should default to low-fidelity brakepoints with larger intervals; node/browser SDKs default to balanced.
- Provide small adapters for existing streaming clients (EventSource / SSE / WebSocket) so they can upgrade with minimal changes.

Telemetry and observability requirements:
- Brakepoint arrival latency histogram (time from model token production to client brakepoint frame emitted).
- Tool-call origin annotation: whether a tool request came from client-initiated callTool or server suggestion.
- Reconnect/resume success rate keyed by resumeToken age and client region.
- Bandwidth delta metric: compare bytes streamed when fidelity=low vs high by client platform.

Operational constraints and safety:
- Brakepoints must be designed so they do not leak hidden sensitive information: annotations should follow existing redaction/Audit rules.
- Tool-call pathway honors per-customer routing/policies and security hooks; SDK should not bypass server-side authorization.
- Limit the number of outstanding tool-call promises per session by default (e.g., 3) to avoid queues/DoS at runtime.

Compatibility and fallback:
- If a client requests brakepoints but runtime does not support it, the server returns a header: X-Session-Protocol: unsupported and falls back to standard streaming. SDK should surface a single event 'protocol_unsupported' and degrade gracefully.
- Breaking changes: brakepoint schema versioning included as meta in frames; default v1. Clients should be tolerant of unknown annotation fields.

Sample decision matrix for fidelity modes:
- low: brakepoint every ~150 tokens or 2000ms, only annotations and tool candidates; text chunks optional. Use for mobile/low bandwidth.
- balanced: brakepoint every ~50 tokens or 800ms, include condensed text checkpoint + annotations. Default for web.
- high: brakepoint every 10 tokens or 200ms, full text and structure. Use for server-to-server agents.

Rollout plan:
- Phase 0 (internal preview, 2 weeks): expose server-side opt-in flag + internal SDK canary in staging. Collect telemetry for brakepoint latency and resume success.
- Phase 1 (beta, 6 weeks): public beta for selected customers with guidance, enable resume tokens and tool-call lightweight router. SDKs include opt-in flag and helpers.
- Phase 2 (general availability, 12 weeks): stable schema v1, instrumentation in Console, default balanced mode for new sessions.

Success metrics:
- Customer-reported incidents related to duplicate tool calls decreases by 60% for beta customers.
- Resume/reconnect success rate > 99% after implementation for sessions using resume token.
- Average bytes transferred per session reduced by 25% for clients opting into low fidelity mode compared to streaming text-only baseline.

Open questions / tradeoffs (notes to self):
- Should brakepoint metadata be signed to prevent tampering on client-side resume? Pros: safety; cons: key management complexity.
- How strict must the runtime be about guaranteeing that resumeToken always maps to exact same semantic state across model rollouts? Minimal guarantee may be acceptable (best-effort).
- How to represent partial structured outputs that are still speculative? Add confidence fields to annotations, but that increases surface area.

Implementation notes for eng teams:
- Serving runtime: add small frame encoder and ensure frame emission is non-blocking. Avoid global barriers when emitting brakepoints.
- Console: surface brakepoint counts, average interval, and average tool-call latencies per model.
- SDKs: implement policy hook with clear default; keep API surface stable and small.

Appendix: short example stream snippet (frame types as newline JSON):
{"type":"chunk","text":"The diagnosis looks"}
{"type":"chunk","text":" like acute viral"}
{"type":"brakepoint","id":"bp-81f2","seq":8,"annotations":[{"kind":"intent","value":"recommend_followup","confidence":0.73}],"resumeToken":"rt-81f2"}
{"type":"chunk","text":" infection, consider rest and fluids."}

References and links: Jira-2047 (product task), PR:678 (proto frames), conf:hosted-api-session-fidelity.

Next steps:
- Product to align with serving-runtime on cheap frame format and resume token TTL.
- Dev-ex to draft SDK helper methods for node/browser/mobile and write migration guide.
- Schedule eng spike for prototype by 2025-02-24.

Notes: draft, expect iterations. This is intentionally lightweight to let teams test ergonomics before adding heavier sequencing guarantees.
